clue.text: Part of the UK restricted by offensive discipline

indicators.note: one thing restricted by another is hemmed in by it, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a push is a military offensive or assault
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland, one part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A region of Britain kept in check by an aggressive campaign of order.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline someone is to penalise them for wrongdoing; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Register one of those in the aviary?

definitions.meaning: to register a vote, or a count of votes cast

definitions.text: one of those in the aviary?
definitions.meaning: a parrot, traditionally called Polly or ...

explanation.definitionFit: A poll is a ballot or register of votes, and also a pet name for a parrot.

clue.text: Call at table, suggesting preference for sirloin or T-bone?

definitions.meaning: a bid in bridge, played at a card table, proposing no suit as trumps

definitions.text: suggesting preference for sirloin or T-bone?
definitions.meaning: read as no rump, a diner refusing the rump cut and choosing another steak

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into 'no T-rump' or 'no rump': someone ordering sirloin or T-bone is passing on rump steak.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a contract with no trump suit is a standard call made at the card table.

clue.text: Treats mostly set up in glasses

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed in the glasses

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the letters read upward, backwards
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: laid means set, as a table is laid

explanation.surface: Delicacies, for the most part, are arranged in drinking glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treats' looks like a verb but is the plural noun; 'set' is laid as of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Specials are special offers or dishes, treats out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Farm animal in support bandage looking bad-tempered

indicators.note: the farm animal is placed in the bandage, so its letters go inside

parts.note: a sling is a bandage that supports an injured arm
a cow is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A cow with its leg strapped up looks thoroughly cross about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowling means frowning angrily, the face of someone in a bad temper.

clue.text: Made a loss and had to take one's medicine?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for losing money on a deal
someone who fell ill with a chill would literally need to take medicine

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means suffered a financial loss, and literally describes picking up a chill needing remedies.

clue.text: The man on river in dry boat

indicators.note: the man and river go in the dry word

parts.note: dry humour is wry
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man on the river sits in a dry vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge used on rivers.

clue.text: Is little woman full of love good for sexual union?

indicators.note: one piece full of another holds it inside

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Is a small lady, brimming with affection, suitable for a partnership?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' and AMY together make ISAMY, which 'full of' fills with OG.
explanation.definitionFit: Isogamy is reproduction by the fusion of gametes of similar form, a biological term for sexual union.

clue.text: Spooner's Sunday clothes? Not what would normally be seen in the pub

definitions.text: Not what would normally be seen in the pub

indicators.note: Spooner is the Oxford don famed for swapping the starts of words

parts.note: Sunday best is one's finest clothes, so Sunday gives best
gear means clothes

explanation.surface: A pub-goer notes that people's Sunday finery is not the usual sight at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunday clothes are 'best gear'; swap their opening sounds and it sounds like the pub phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest beer is an ale a pub sells temporarily, not part of its usual range.

clue.text: Some Californian wine? It's seen over time as rubbish

indicators.note: the wine measure is seen over, that is covering, the time letter, so the one goes round the other

parts.note: a liter, spelt the American way, is a quantity of wine as measured in California

explanation.surface: A Californian vintage gets labelled trash once it has aged.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling LITER, signalled by 'Californian', is what is needed here, not the British LITRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is discarded waste scattered about, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Plant that's alien to be sure

indicators.note: something alien is strange or foreign, so these letters are turned into an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener insists a certain plant must have come from elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuberose is a fragrant flowering plant of the agave family, grown for perfume.

clue.text: Pre-eminent Heather, the woman featured in tribute after game

indicators.note: the heather and tribute pieces come after the game, so the game letters go first

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for rugby union, a game
ling is another name for common heather

indicators.note: the woman is featured in the tribute, so her letters sit within it

parts.note: a toast is a tribute drunk to someone
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A leading Heather gets a woman's toast after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a variant of 'ruling the roost', the version some dictionaries also accept.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in charge and dominant over everyone else is said to be in this position, being pre-eminent.

clue.text: Pastor doing wrong is far from completely OK

indicators.note: doing wrong points to letters put the wrong way

explanation.surface: A clergyman behaving badly is hardly beyond reproach.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls the curate's egg, good only here and there.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something as acceptable only in places means it is patchy, far from wholly satisfactory.

clue.text: Horses shock ducks — aggressive group going in?

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
a duck is a score of nought, so ducks are two Os
the SAS is the Special Air Service, an aggressive British military unit

explanation.surface: Horses are startled when birds and a special forces squad charge in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in?' is a link: the SAS are the troop that goes in on raids.
explanation.definitionFit: Appaloosas are a spotted breed of horse from North America.

clue.text: Something to treat disease? It's carried up by a nurse, frenzied maiden

indicators.note: carried by means held by, so the reversed piece goes inside
frenzied means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: in a down answer carried up means lifted upward, read backwards

parts.note: the word it, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: Something medicinal is lifted by a nurse and a hysterical girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' supplies only IT; the 's is a link. 'by' means held by, so the reversed piece goes into the scrambled nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is a serum containing antibodies, given to treat or prevent disease.

clue.text: Instrument not a provider of accurate information, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear points to a word spoken, so the description is matched by sound

parts.words: not a provider of accurate information
parts.note: someone who does not give accurate information is a liar

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is said to be an unreliable source of facts.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is a stringed instrument, a small harp of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Talk about bad flood!

indicators.note: the talk word goes about the bad one, around it

parts.note: to spout is to talk at length
ill means bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: Discussion of a terrible deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour forth in a rush, as a crowd from doors, is to flood out.

clue.text: Struggle with material in short supply

indicators.note: short means cut, so the material word loses its last letter

parts.note: toile is a fine linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric is scarce and making do is a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to labour hard, to struggle with a task.

clue.text: A sinner being troubled, more unstable

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer with a guilty conscience grows increasingly unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Insaner is the comparative of insane, so more mentally unstable.

clue.text: Breaker of promise, thrice ultimately (NT)

parts.note: the apostle in the New Testament who swore he would stand by Jesus but in the end denied knowing him three times

explanation.walkthrough: NT is the New Testament; the apostle vowed loyalty at the Last Supper and then denied Jesus three times before the cock crowed.
explanation.definitionFit: This apostle, also called Cephas, is the disciple whose triple denial is told in all four Gospels.

clue.text: Only clips a vehicle

definitions.meaning: a film preview consisting only of short excerpts
a wheeled unit towed behind a car or lorry

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cinema preview made of excerpts and a towed wagon.

clue.text: Exhausted, only 10% there at the end in capacity

indicators.note: as Roman numerals, 50 is a tenth of 500, so the final letter is swapped for one worth a tenth

parts.note: bushed is informal for exhausted

explanation.surface: A worn-out drinker is barely present by closing time, holding very little.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals and L is 50, a tenth of it, so the final D becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is a unit of dry capacity equal to eight gallons.

clue.text: Pasquale, inside working, using long obscure words

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work and reshaped

parts.note: the setter's pseudonym, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter himself, busily at work within, is fond of long words.
explanation.walkthrough: Pasquale is the setter himself, a self-reference: he is known for unusual vocabulary, so the clue reads as a whole-clue confession.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes long-winded speech full of polysyllables, literally a foot and a half long in Latin.

clue.text: Victim of attack to ask for divine help, audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: to pray is to ask God for help

explanation.surface: Someone attacked calls on heaven for aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey is the quarry an animal hunts, a victim of an attack.

clue.text: Farmers managed half-hearted thanks

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, so ran is managed

indicators.note: the word loses half of its heart, one of its two central letters

parts.note: cheers is an informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: The farmers ran things and offered only a lukewarm thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranchers run cattle ranches, so they are a kind of farmer.

clue.text: One running up to man in helmet or hat?

definitions.text: One running up to man in helmet
definitions.meaning: in cricket the player delivering the ball runs up towards the batsman, who wears a helmet
a hard felt hat with a rounded crown, the British businessman's hat

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the player who delivers the ball runs in towards the batsman; the same word is also a hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the cricketer who delivers the ball and a dome-crowned felt hat.

clue.text: Painter has knocked back drink, belonging to a celebrated group

indicators.note: knocked back suggests something thrown in reverse, so the drink word is read backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
the A-list is the set of most celebrated people

explanation.surface: A painter downed a drink and joined the in-crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A muralist is an artist who paints murals, large paintings on walls.

clue.text: Harmony's last thing on the shop floor

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it, so this letter comes after

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: the last thing of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Harmony's final item sits on the shop floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, a floor.
